newsitem.title: GERMANY: Top German shares generally lower in bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: Top German shares generally lower in bourse trade.

text.p: Germany's top 30 blue-chip shares were all in negative territory in floor trade on Friday, with the exception of retailer Metro, as uncertainty over currency union hit trading sentiment.
Dealers said the clash between Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Germany's powerful Bundesbank the valuation of gold reserves fed into market sentiment to drag the DAX index lower.
The DAX index was down 50 points, or 1.37 percent, at 3,586.422 points in bourse trade, which dealers said was characterised by low volumes.

"People are looking to see what's next in the row between Waigel and the Bundesbank, mainly focusing on its effect on the dollar/mark exchange rate. Most trade is coming chiefly from the derivatives side," a Frankfurt trader said.
The overall picture for shares was a downbeat one. German Bunds were well down early on, while Wall Street closed down 27.05 points at 7,330.18 overnight.

Speculation about a possible victory for the left in Sunday's elections in France added to the gloomy picture for German equities. The spectre of interest rate hikes abroad and at home further clouded the horizon.
"There is also s peculation about possible interest rate rises in Japan, which could feed through into a clear rise in German rates in coming months," said the trader.

"Generally we are seeing very quiet volumes today. There aren't that many people around, as a lot are still on holiday. We should see a generous level of support between 3,550 and 3,500 points," he said.
Corporate news was generally thin on the ground.

Commerzbank AG was due to hold its annual general meeting in the morning. Shares in Germany's third largest commercial bank were down 1.10 marks at 50.10 marks in early bourse, despite issuing an upbeat earnings outlook for 1997.
Carmaker Volkswagen AG said that its China joint venture had recorded a profit for the first time. Volkswagen shares were down 10 marks at 1,119.50 marks, slightly outperforming the overall market.
Retailer Metro AG was the only gainer among the blue-chips, up one mark at 187 marks.
